key_insight: PPy-PVA hydrogel geometry provides an additional lever for tuning drug transport by altering microstructure and local electric fields.
engineering_relevance: Geometry-driven hydrogel design could enable tunable iontophoretic delivery without separately adjusting current density for each design.
method: Fabricated BSA-loaded hydrogels in five geometries, including Hilbert curve-based designs.
Evaluated electric fields with finite element analysis and microstructure with scanning electron microscopy.
Measured passive and iontophoretic transport using Franz diffusion cells with artificial membranes.
evidence_signal: The five geometries showed distinct release, flux, and permeability profiles; average iontophoretic permeability was (3.80 ± 1.93) × 10⁻⁵, with units unspecified in the abstract.
watch_item: Artificial-membrane testing does not establish performance or safety in skin, and the abstract reports no AI surrogate model.
paper_title: Geometry-Dependent Properties of Physically Crosslinked PPy-PVA Hydrogels Enable Tunable Iontophoretic Drug Delivery
